news.body: The company's share price has been volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 75% of Indian stocks, typically moving 8.7% a week. This is considered a minor risk. Share price volatility indicates the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent. It also increases the risk of potential losses in the short term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. news.title: Investor sentiment improves as stock rises 16%
news.body: After last week's 16% share price gain to ₹512, the stock trades at a trailing P/E ratio of 16.5x. Average trailing P/E is 23x in the Trade Distributors industry in India. Total returns to shareholders of 82% over the past three years.

news.title: New minor risk - Profit margin trend
news.body: The company's profit margins are lower than last year and have reduced by more than 30%. Net profit margin: 48% Last year net profit margin: 131% This is considered a minor risk. A large drop in profit margin could indicate the company does not have strong competitive advantages or it is yet to establish itself and its core business. Even if it is a well established business, this may make it a much riskier investment than one that has a combination of proven competitive advantages and a stable or growing profit margin. Currently, the following risks have been identified for the company: Minor Risks Paying a dividend despite having no free cash flows. Profit margins are more than 30% lower than last year (48% net profit margin).

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹31.03 (vs ₹57.82 in FY 2025)
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹31.03 (down from ₹57.82 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹4.53b (up 46% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹2.18b (down 46% from FY 2025). news.title: MSTC Limited Recommends Final Dividend for the Financial Year 2025-2026
news.body: MSTC Limited at its board meeting held on 29 May 2026, subject to the approval of the shareholders at the upcoming Annual General Meeting of the Company to be held on 24 September 2026, recommended final dividend of INR 8.10 per equity share, (i.e. 81 % on the paid-up equity share capital) for the Financial Year 2025-2026. The final dividend would be paid within 30 days from the date of its declaration at the 61st AGM of the Company. The final dividend is in addition to the Interim Dividend paid for the financial year 2025-2026. The record date for payment of final dividend shall be intimated in due course.

news.title: New minor risk - Dividend sustainability
news.body: The dividend is not well covered by cash flows. Cash payout ratio: 153% Dividend yield: 2.5% This is considered a minor risk. Dividends are ultimately paid out of the company's available cash reserves. Companies that pay out too much of their cash flow are at risk of having to reduce or cut their dividend in future. If cash flow growth slows or cash flows fall, then there may not be enough cash reserves to maintain the same dividend. Or in extreme cases, companies may opt to take on debt to maintain the dividend. This risk is mitigated by the fact the dividend is covered by earnings, however, cash flows are generally more important.
